title: Meridiani demo: Endeavour rim corridor survey and replanning
summary: The drone surveys an uncertain corridor, finds a scarp, the first route is invalidated and the astronaut is replanned around it, reaches goal B and returns to base.
disclaimer: Terrain: NASA HiRISE DEM crop of Endeavour crater's west rim along Opportunity's traverse (real, provisional, 8 m display grid averaged from its 1 m DEM). Rover stop markers: real Opportunity stops (NASA). Mission, budgets and the corridor scarp are simulated or synthetic; POIs C and D are real Opportunity science sites (NASA), visited here in a simulated story. Rover (1 m/s) and drone (4 m/s, 40 m up) motion is simulated; the rover is faster than real hardware (Perseverance about 4.2 cm/s), the drone below the Ingenuity top speed (about 5 m/s, flown at 10-24 m). Not EVA-certified limits, not a planner output.

ai_disclosure.scope: Fixture generator script and replay fixture structure; the simulated mission, routes and events are generated data, not observations.
ai_disclosure.observational_data: Only the terrain heights come from NASA/USGS data; everything else here is simulated.

sources: MRO HiRISE DEM of Endeavour crater west rim, 1 m, NASA JPL Mars Trek (USGS Astrogeology / HiRISE and CTX teams). File DEM_1m_Endeavour_Crater_isis3_2017-04-14.tif, 703735672 bytes, SHA-256 9732dfc953fcf5d70743f7435ba96b6222c9e43d7639430d044047c5fda85649.
Product page https://trek.nasa.gov/mars/. Native resolution 1 m. Not verified here: NASA planetary data served by JPL Mars Trek, see the Trek product page for usage terms.

Crop: 950 x 425 cells of 8 m centred at -2.2679 N, -5.369 E, box average of 8 x 8 source pixels, then bilinear resampling onto a local tangent ENU grid (east = R cos(lat) dlon, north = R dlat); 8 m cells. PROVISIONAL, made by the frontend until the data owner delivers the processed package.
SYNTHETIC: a scarp was added to the hidden evaluator reference to create an adverse case. It does not exist in the NASA terrain data.
ILLUSTRATIVE: uncertainty (sigma), budgets, speeds and consumption rates are assumptions of a simulated mission.

Real Opportunity science site: Botany Bay, contact science on the rock target Gnarlaroo, Endeavour Crater, Cape York, Botany Bay, sol 3332. Placed at the rover's published position at the time (stop 172_1348), on the nearest drivable cell within 12 m. Source: PDS Geosciences Node, MER Contact Science Target List (urn:nasa:pds:mer_cs_target_list), first contact-science sol per feature.

Real Opportunity science site nearest to goal B that the astronaut can walk to: NW Bench, contact science on the rock target Homestake, Endeavour Crater, Cape York, sol 2764, at the rover's published position (stop 162_27). 0.99 km on foot from goal B (project slope limit 20 degrees). Source: PDS Geosciences Node, MER Contact Science Target List (urn:nasa:pds:mer_cs_target_list), first contact-science sol per feature.

Chosen by the demo generator with a published NASA criterion, not a NASA site: the 1 km x 1 km area with the gentlest ground of the NASA DEM that meets the civil-engineering slope criterion of NASA's 2015 human Exploration Zone rubric (slope under 10 degrees at the 1 km scale: 0.3 degrees; within 5 km of the landing site, here base A: 3.68 km). Mean 8 m slope 0.4 degrees, 0 % of cells above 10 degrees. The rubric's ~50 km2 area and sparse rocks are not checked (crop too small, no rock-abundance data); water ice and hydrated minerals are not assessed (no such product imported).
